Perfect! White wins Black's rook. The main line is: **Rxh3+ Kg4 Rg3+ Kf5 Rxg8** winning the rook. This is an **attraction** (or deflection) motif—by capturing the pawn with check, White forces the king to g4, which allows Rg3+ to dislodge it, and then the rook on g8 becomes loose and undefended.

**Best move:** Rxh3+

**Main line:** Rxh3+ Kg4 Rg3+ Kf5 Rxg8

**Motif:** attraction (or deflection)

**Coaching note:**
When your opponent has an undefended rook or piece far from the action, check if you can force the king away by attacking it repeatedly. Here, Rxh3+ attracts the king forward with check. After Black moves to Kg4, Rg3+ forces it again—now the rook on g8 is undefended and lost. Always check if captures with tempo (checks) can win material by forcing the king onto worse squares.
